topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the opening framing, outlining the course structure and intended learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Genetic, cellular, and structural disruptions in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer arises from accumulating genetic alterations, failed differentiation programs, and lost tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how benign and malignant tumors are distinguished clinically and histologically through local invasion, metastatic spread, and stepwise tissue progression.

topics.label: Conventions and exceptions of tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard naming rules and notable exceptions used to classify tumors based on their cell lineage and malignant potential.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological mechanisms and systemic consequences by which primary and metastatic tumors produce illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across human populations and multicellular species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor frequency and cancer mortality across tissues, human demographics, and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles, histology, and limitations of clinical cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, tissue-level detection methods, and clinical effectiveness of screening programs across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the closing framing, summarizing learning objectives and offering practical session reminders.
